title: Large Language Models as Digital Twins: a Distribution-Aware Questionnaire-Based Evaluation
abstract: arXiv:2611.16586v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: This paper investigates whether Large Language Models can answer a personality questionnaire as a specific individual would. Given a user's social-media posts, the model completes the BFI-2-60 Big Five questionnaire as that user. The predicted responses are converted into trait scores and compared with the user's actual scores. We evaluate GPT-4, Gemma, Llama 3.1, and Mistral on the MyPersonality dataset. To determine whether predictions reflect information from the user's writing, we compare them with answers produced without user text and with values derived from general population tendencies. We measure prediction error across all users and separately for individuals with low, intermediate, and high trait scores. We also test whether an LLM can express an explicit personality profile when given only the target Big Five scores, without user text, and examine how predictions change as more text is provided. translated_title: 大语言模型作为数字孪生：一种分布感知的问卷式评估
translated_abstract: 本文研究大语言模型能否像特定个体那样回答人格问卷。给定用户的社交媒体帖子，模型以该用户的身份完成 BFI-2-60 大五人格问卷，并将预测的回答转换为特质分数，与用户的实际分数进行比较。研究者在 MyPersonality 数据集上评估了 GPT-4、Gemma、Llama 3.1 和 Mistral。为了确定预测是否反映了用户文本中的信息，他们将预测结果与无用户文本时生成的回答以及基于一般人群倾向得出的数值进行对比。研究测量了所有用户的预测误差，并分别针对低、中、高特质得分的个体进行分析。此外，研究还测试了在仅给定目标大五人格分数（无用户文本）的情况下，大语言模型能否表达出明确的人格特征，并考察了随着提供更多文本时预测结果的变化。结果表明，用户文本……
tldr: 该论文评估了GPT-4、Gemma、Llama 3.1和Mistral等大语言模型能否基于用户社交媒体帖子以“数字孪生”方式预测其在BFI-2-60大五人格问卷上的回答，并通过无用户文本和人群基线等分布感知对比方法，验证预测是否真正利用了用户写作中的信息。
en_tdlr: This paper evaluates whether LLMs (GPT-4, Gemma, Llama 3.1, Mistral) can act as "digital twins" by predicting users' BFI-2-60 Big Five personality questionnaire responses from their social media posts, using distribution-aware baselines (no-user-text answers and population tendencies) to verify whether predictions genuinely leverage information from users' writing.
